Now that we have DML/DMR sets of interest, we need to know more information about where they’re located in the genome, including genomic distribution (representation among introns, exons, intergenetic regions, etc.) and, for intragenic features, the function of those genes. Here I’ll build a Uniprot/Swissprot lookup table of GO terms for the C. virginica genome (3.0) so that I can functionally annotate our features of interest

I largely followed the [Roberts Lab Handbook’s GO/GOslim workflow](https://robertslab.github.io/resources/bio-Annotation/#retrieve-go-terms-from-uniprot-using-swissprot-ids)

The basic workflow is as follows:

1.  Obtain the *C.virginica* proteome and BLAST it against the SwissProt database to obtain top-match functional annotations for each protien

2.  Map the *C.virginica* protiens to corresponding genes

3.  Using each gene's mapped SwissProt ID, retrieve corresponding GO terms from Uniprot

4.  Map obtained GO terms to GOslims

5.  Compile all of this into a lookup table. For each gene we can see Gene ID, Protein ID, SPID, BLAST stats (% identity match, evalue, etc.), Protein name, organism name, and GO terms (BP, CC, MF, GOslim terms)

Note that this approach, which initially BLASTs against the *C. virginica* proteome, inherently limits our annotation to protein-coding genes -- noncoding features (tRNA, lncRNA, etc.) are excluded.

Full code can be found at [14-functional-annotation](https://github.com/shedurkin/ceasmallr/blob/main/code/14-functional-annotation.md). <a href="https://robertslab.github.io/resources/Agentic-Coding-Tools/#five-level-rubric"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/AI%20Use-Level%202%20Drafting%2FCoding-yellowgreen" alt="AI Use Level 2: AI-assisted drafting or coding"/></a>
